Subject: SIG Q14 follow-up — KV namespace and backup scope

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the SIG packet. We're working through Q14 (KV namespaces / key attribution for backups) and a couple of items were ambiguous for our reviewers:

- Do Redwood-managed backups include per-customer KV namespace identifiers in metadata stored off-box?
- If a customer elects private deployment, does the backup chain still rely on a Redwood-hosted staging area for snapshots?

Can you confirm the precise scope and where any namespace identifiers appear in the backup artifacts? If convenient, we'd appreciate a short call to walk through the evidence you can provide (screenshots, config snippets).

Best,
Alice Ng
Senior InfoSec Analyst
SummitBank

P: +1-415-555-0129

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SIG Q14 follow-up — KV namespace and backup scope

Alice — thanks for the note. Short answers up front:

- Redwood-managed backups do not embed customer-facing KV namespace identifiers in off-box metadata by default; internal shard IDs are used and are not meaningful outside our system.
- For Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem), snapshots are customer-local unless the customer opts into Redwood-managed snapshot replication — in that case we stage encrypted blobs in a customer-isolated bucket and maintain only an opaque manifest entry.

That said, I want to be explicit in how we word this for SIG responders. Stephanie, can you review the attached draft excerpt (SIG_Q14_KV_namespace_excerpt.pdf) and confirm the evidence we can commit? Monica — can you check whether we have a sanitized S3 manifest screenshot we can use?

If it helps, I'm available for a 30-minute call today at 2pm PT to walk the SummitBank team through the artifact layout and the manifest fields.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer

Subject: Re: SIG Q14 follow-up — KV namespace and backup scope — notes & confirmation

Hi Alice / Tom — thanks for the call earlier. Notes and agreed interpretation below (summarized for SIG Q14 response):

1) Backup artifact structure (high level)
- Snapshot consists of: encrypted blob(s) + manifest (JSON).
- Manifest fields: internal_manifest_id (opaque), shard_map (internal shard ids), created_at, checksum, encryption_key_id (alias-to-kms-key)
- No customer-facing namespace string or human-readable customer_id is present in the manifest when Redwood-managed backups are used. We verified this against the sanitized example we shared on the call.

2) Private / VPC deployments
- By default, snapshots remain in customer-controlled storage. If a customer opts into Redwood-managed replication for DR, we stage snapshots into an isolated bucket owned by the customer account and only retain an opaque manifest pointer. No customer namespace strings are introduced by this flow.

3) Evidence provided
- Attached: sanitized manifest PDF and a link to the short recording of the demo (meeting-recording-link.txt).
- Action: Redwood will include the sanitized manifest PDF as evidence for SIG Q14 and update the SIG response language to explicitly state \"no customer-facing KV namespace is embedded in backup manifests\".

4) Follow-ups
- Monica will add the sanitized manifest to the secure evidence bundle in the shared Drive (link above).
- Stephanie will update the SIG answer text and route through legal for a final sign-off before we return to the customer.

If that summary looks right, we'll send the final SIG Q14 response by EOD Thursday (2026-12-03).

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Sr. Solutions Engineer — Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
